clue.text: The smart money, not much of it in the county, isn't taking the risk

parts.note: smart in the sense of stylish means chic

indicators.note: in tells us the coin sits inside the county

parts.note: Kent is an English county in the south-east
a sou is an old French coin of tiny value, so a very small amount of money

explanation.surface: Someone with clever money in a county is reluctant to gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The smart money' looks like one phrase but splits; the coin goes 'in' the county, and 'The' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To back out of something through fear is the idiom 'chicken out', so someone doing so avoids the gamble.

clue.text: 1 across should do so, with disastrous consequences?

definitions.text: 1 across should do so, with disastrous consequences?

parts.words: 1 across should do so, with disastrous consequences
parts.note: the poultry of the across answer return to their perch at night, and the idiom says bad deeds rebound on the doer

explanation.surface: Those who back out will suffer the consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: The across answer begins with poultry; the proverb says chickens return to roost, meaning past actions bring their own punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes wrongdoing rebounding disastrously, which is what roosting fowl from the cross-referenced answer would literally do.

clue.text: West's out of season, getting put into a hole

indicators.note: out of tells us the compass letter leaves the season's name

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Timothy West is unemployed in the off-season and finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: West recurs as a theme (the actor Timothy West), but here it is just the compass point W.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, which means putting a body into a hole in the ground.

clue.text: Surgery for the listener?

definitions.meaning: minimally invasive operating through a tiny opening
the opening in a door where an eavesdropper puts an ear

explanation.walkthrough: Keyhole surgery is minimally invasive surgery; an eavesdropper listens at a door's opening for the key.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyhole surgery is the common term for laparoscopic operations, and eavesdroppers famously listen at that door opening.

clue.text: Roving detectives take a day to turn up

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: Wandering police officers take a day off before arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses CIDAMON, written top to bottom, to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples move from place to place, so they are roving rather than settled.

clue.text: Paint with quality sharpener

parts.note: oils are oil paints, the medium of a painting
tone is the quality of a sound or colour

explanation.surface: An artist uses paint along with a fine tool for honing.
explanation.definitionFit: A whetstone lubricated with oil is used to sharpen blades, so it is a sharpener.

clue.text: Slab, board, list? It ends in a square

definitions.text: Slab, board, list? It ends in a square

parts.words: Slab, board, list? It ends in a square
parts.note: slab, board and list can each mean a table, so the word appears three times, and that multiplication chart finishes on thirty-six, six squared

explanation.surface: Three flat objects listed, then a remark about one finishing on a square.
explanation.walkthrough: A table can be a slab, a board (as in food) or a list. The times table of three ends with 3 x 12 = 36, a perfect square.
explanation.definitionFit: The multiplication table for three runs up to thirty-six, which is six squared.

clue.text: A fabric as you like?

parts.note: twill is a woven fabric with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: A piece of cloth suitable for any purpose you choose.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at will means doing it whenever or however one pleases.

clue.text: See 14
West's turned it to a Dream part — your first?

indicators.note: turned tells us the little word it is written backwards

parts.note: Moth is a fairy in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of your

explanation.surface: An actor turned a role in a Shakespeare play into his debut.
explanation.walkthrough: Timothy West is a British actor, the theme of several clues. 'it' turned gives TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor West's first name, so the clue's surname stands in for the forename.

clue.text: Complaint of West Side girl about US city

indicators.note: about means the girl's name surrounds the city

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of the musical West Side Story
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A girl from a famous musical grumbles about an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Side' is not part of the theme of Timothy West here: it points to the musical West Side Story.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an illness, and this is a mosquito-borne disease.

clue.text: Writer goes first to the forest

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, so the first
Sherwood is the English forest of Robin Hood fame

explanation.surface: An author goes ahead of everyone into the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes' and 'to' simply join the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an English novelist, author of Goodbye to Berlin.

clue.text: Coming up in Rome,3 and 6

parts.note: tre is Italian for three, as spoken in Rome
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Something rising in the Italian capital, with two numbers attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are not cross-references here: 3 in Italian, 6 in Roman numerals. The definition refers to the fountain's water rising.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trevi Fountain in Rome sends water up from its jets, a famous sight where coins are thrown.

clue.text: Not a member in sight? Well I'm blessed!

indicators.note: in sight says the letters are visible within the exclamation

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise about no member being visible.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'weLL I'M BLESSed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a member of the body, so being without any limbs means having no member.

clue.text: Seamen worry airmen twice with energy and tender loving care

indicators.note: to worry something is to disturb it, so these letters get rearranged
twice says the word airmen is used two times

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Sailors fret about air force men, though both look after each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles AIRMEN; with E and TLC, 'worry' rearranges the sixteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The merchant navy's seamen were formerly called by this name, the commercial fleet rather than warships.

clue.text: Sound beast carrying rubbish carrier

indicators.note: carrying here means the beast has the other pieces loaded on in front

parts.note: orts are scraps or leftovers, food refuse
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
an ox is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A noisy animal hauls a bin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound doctrine or opinion is conventional and accepted, which is the meaning of orthodox.

clue.text: Utility as concern of urology?

definitions.meaning: a public water supply plant is a utility
colloquially the urinary system, what urologists treat

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a water-supply plant and, colloquially, the bladder and urinary tract.

clue.text: Deer — tha'sh a shame!

indicators.note: the slurred spelling signals a drunk's pronunciation

parts.note: what a pity is another way of saying that's a shame

explanation.surface: A tipsy speaker laments something about a deer.
explanation.walkthrough: Slurred, 'what a pity' comes out as the name of the deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The wapiti is the North American elk, a large deer.

clue.text: Marsupial to work with large amount

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
OS stands for outsize, a large clothing size
a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: An animal is set to labour for a big sum.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is an American marsupial that carries young in a pouch.

clue.text: Vegetable with no date's a date …

parts.note: kale is a leafy green vegetable
n.d. abbreviates no date in references, plus the S of the 's

explanation.surface: A green with no sell-by date is itself a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs into the next clue, where 'a date' supplies part of its answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The calends were the first day of the month in the Roman calendar, so a specific date.

clue.text: See 13
… on which the home counties are composed

parts.note: the counties around London are in the south-east, SE
the dots carry on from the previous clue, whose last words a date supply this piece

explanation.surface: The day on which the counties round London were written.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with 18: 'a date … on which the home counties are' gives a DATE with SE on it. The Home Counties are those surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedate person is calm and composed, unhurried in manner.

clue.text: Fish for bird

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish of rivers and lakes
a bar or branch for a bird to rest on

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spiny-finned fish and a resting place for a bird.

clue.text: Constrained to go to bed with Gila monster

indicators.note: monster suggests something deformed, so these letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Forced to sleep beside a venomous lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' and 'with' are links; the Gila monster is a venomous American lizard, and 'monster' does double service in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: To be obligated is to be bound by duty, hence constrained.

clue.text: A drop on the way to the drain, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.words: on the way to the drain
parts.note: water runs along a gutter to reach the drain

explanation.surface: Water drips along its path to the sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the ending sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutta is Latin for a drop, used in pharmacy and architecture.

clue.text: Talk of genuine computer system the high point of the island

definitions.text: the high point of the island

indicators.note: talk of signals the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: genuine means true
DOS is the Disk Operating System for computers

explanation.surface: Discussion of real software as the island's best feature.
explanation.definitionFit: The Troodos range holds Mount Olympus, the highest peak on Cyprus.

clue.text: The whole lot? Far from it

definitions.meaning: cryptically, everything is not merely a small piece
an emphatic denial, not in the least

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means not at all, and cryptically the whole is not a mere fragment.

clue.text: Mobile parts of traditional sermon

parts.note: a sermon traditionally opens on a scriptural text
and delivers a message to the congregation

explanation.surface: Portable sections of an old-style preacher's address.
explanation.definitionFit: A short message sent by mobile phone, so mobile here is the phone's communication.
